sender: Superior Court Jury Services Office, Valley Crest Judicial District
headline: This is a jury duty summons telling you to report on {{DATE:+10}}.
summary: The Superior Court Jury Services Office picked you at random to serve as a juror. You must report on {{WD:+10}}, {{DATE:+10}} at 7:45 AM. You must also respond to the court before that date. You can confirm, or ask for a delay or an excuse.

deadline.what_is_due: Respond to the summons (confirm, or ask for a postponement or excuse) before you report. Report in person at 7:45 AM on this date. The letter does not give an earlier response deadline, so respond as soon as you can.

if_ignored: The letter says you could be fined up to $1,500 and be ordered to come to a court hearing (called an order to show cause) for not obeying a court order. Responding is quick and usually avoids all of this.

action_steps.title: Respond to the court now
action_steps.detail: Go to www.jurysvc-sample.org and enter your Juror ID JX-302-8817. Or call (818) 555-0143, Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM. Confirm you will serve, or ask for a postponement or excuse.

action_steps.title: Ask for help if you need it
action_steps.detail: If you need a language interpreter or a disability accommodation, say so when you respond. If you need a different date, ask for a postponement. Have your reason ready, such as work, health, travel or caring for someone.

action_steps.title: Check again the night before
action_steps.detail: On {{WD:+9}}, {{MD:+9}}, after 5:00 PM, call or check the website to make sure you still need to come in.

action_steps.title: Get ready to go
action_steps.detail: Bring this summons and a photo ID. Report to the Jury Assembly Room, Valley Crest Courthouse, 88 Courthouse Way, Fairview Glen, CA 91299, by 7:45 AM on {{WD:+10}}, {{DATE:+10}}. Parking is in Lot B.

action_steps.title: Tell your employer
action_steps.detail: Let your employer know about the dates. The letter says they may not fire you for jury service. You will be paid $15 per day starting on the second day, plus mileage.

red_flags.text: The letter gives no separate response deadline. It only says to respond before your report date. Do not wait until the last day.
The phone number in the letter is the same as the one in the header. If you want to double-check, find the court's number on its official website.

reasons: It does not ask for money, gift cards, wire transfers, SSN or bank logins.
It gives a Juror ID, a clear report date, time and place, and normal court instructions.
The fine mentioned is for not responding, not a payment demand. It does not threaten immediate arrest.
Tip: to be safe, look up your court's jury page yourself and enter your Juror ID there. Never give your SSN or pay money by phone for jury duty.
